concepts.def: Maslow's five-tier pyramid from physiological to self-actualisation.
Rogers — closeness between self and ideal self.
Learning from observed consequences for others.

walkthroughs.body_html: Maslow (1943) argued people work up a five-level pyramid: physiological, safety, love/belonging, esteem and self-actualisation. Lower needs must be met first. Only around 2% achieve self-actualisation — humanistic psychology centres on this growth.

Rogers (1959) emphasised congruence between actual self and ideal self. Parents giving only conditional positive regard create conditions of worth that prevent self-actualisation. Client-centred therapy gives unconditional positive regard.

Bandura, Ross & Ross (1961) showed children watching adults beat a Bobo doll imitated those behaviours; children seeing non-aggressive models did not. SLT introduced four mediational processes — attention, retention, reproduction, motivation — bridging behaviourism and cognition.
